title: Resources: Addressable Content for a Stateless Server

questions.question: A client sends resources/read for a URI the server does not recognize. What must a conformant 2026-07-28 server return?
options: A JSON-RPC error -32602 whose data names the requested URI
A JSON-RPC error -32601 because the read method is unknown
A complete result whose contents array is left empty
A tool execution error result with isError set to true
questions.explanation: A missing resource is JSON-RPC error -32602 with data.uri identifying the request; an empty contents array is disallowed because it cannot distinguish absence from an empty document.

questions.question: Before SEP-2164, servers commonly used -32002 for a missing resource. What should a 2026-07-28 server do with that code?
options: Emit -32002 on stdio and -32602 on Streamable HTTP transports
Use -32602 going forward; still accept -32002 from legacy peers
Treat -32002 and -32602 as two unrelated, unrecognized error codes
Emit -32002 whenever the resource lives under the file scheme
questions.explanation: SEP-2164 standardized resource-not-found as -32602, the ordinary Invalid params code; a 2026-07-28 server must not emit -32002 itself, though a client should still recognize it from an older peer.

questions.question: A resources/read call succeeds with resultType complete. Which two fields must the result carry alongside contents?
options: nextCursor and pageSize, so the client can page through content
supportedVersions and capabilities, so the client can renegotiate its version
ttlMs and cacheScope, the freshness and sharing hints for caching
inputRequests and requestState, so the client can retry with input
questions.explanation: Resources/read is one of the six cacheable operations; a complete result must carry ttlMs, how long the client may treat it as fresh, and cacheScope, public or private.

questions.question: A server holds a document that only it can reach; no client could fetch the same bytes straight from the open web. Which URI scheme guidance applies?
options: Use https, since any URI can be marked directly fetchable
Use git only for resources kept under real version control
Use https, then a header tells clients to skip it
Use file or a custom scheme; keep https for direct fetches
questions.explanation: The specification reserves https for content a client can fetch directly from the web on its own; content only the server can reach should use file, git, or a scheme of the server's own.

questions.question: A resource read returns a note that belongs to one authenticated user. Which cacheScope keeps that read from leaking into another user's cache?
options: private, so cached copies never cross authorization contexts
public, because notes are small enough to share safely
private, but only when the transport is stdio
public, combined with a very short ttlMs value
questions.explanation: cacheScope private means a cached response may be reused for the same authorization context but must never be shared across different callers, exactly what user-specific content needs.

questions.question: A client wants to learn when a specific resource changes. What does it send under the 2026-07-28 revision?
options: server/discover with a capabilities.resources.subscribe flag set to true
subscriptions/listen with the URI listed under resourceSubscriptions
resources/subscribe naming the URI, as in earlier revisions
resources/read repeated on a short polling interval
questions.explanation: The standalone resources/subscribe request was retired; a client now sends subscriptions/listen with the resourceSubscriptions filter naming the URIs it wants updates for.
